newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close sharply lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a drubbing Friday, imitating Wall Street, and the loss may have eroded the market's underlying strength, dealers said.
"We could be facing a change in trend," said Rodrigo Diz of Velox traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index dived 2.8 percent to a 10-week low of 686.15, boosting weekly losses to five percent.
"The bolsa was lashed by the dive in New York and it may take another loss of seven or eight percent before institutional investors return," said Gabriel Armando of brokers Galicia Valores.

Traders said the Dow's 2.3 percent drop and the jump in U.S. long bond yields, which hit 7.19 percent but closed at 7.17 percent against 7.11 percent at the opening, dictated the pace of events on the bolsa.

"The good news is that if local private pension funds weren't heavily invested in the market, we would have suffered a much greater fall considering how stocks fared abroad," Armando said, noting the reduced volatility on the bolsa.
Floor volume eased to 15.9 million pesos from 16.9 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 77.1 million from 90.4 million Thursday.
The broad market lost 2.2 percent, with winners trouncing losers 46 to two and eight issues closing flat.

Heaviest main-tier losers were steelmakers Acindar and Siderar, which tumbled 4.3 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively, and banks Bansud and Banco de Galicia, down 4.1 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively.

The day's worst performer was Pepsi bottler Baesa, which reeled nearly 40 percent on the company's dire financial situation. Baesa went untraded on the bolsa Thursday, when it started its plunge on Wall Street.
